strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifying that binary forgery masks lack interpretability and proposing textual explanations is a valid research direction
Substantial dataset contribution: 128,303 image-text pairs with thoughtful annotation pipeline including inconsistency inspection, quality control, and iterative refinement
Diverse manipulation coverage: Three different manipulation methods (face swapping, transformer-based and diffusion-based inpainting) with comprehensive dataset statistics
Reasonable technical approach: Sensible two-stage training with coordinate convolution and integration of SAM/InstructBLIP
Commitment to reproducibility: Authors promise to release dataset, code, and pretrained checkpoints
weaknesses: Critical FPN bottleneck severely undermines core claims: FPN achieves only 41% PLM, and the CIDEr gap between FPN-GT (48.1) and actual FPN (21.5) shows 55% performance drop, directly limiting interpretation quality

No human evaluation of interpretation quality: Despite claiming interpretability, the paper relies only on automatic metrics (BLEU/METEOR/CIDEr) without validating whether explanations are actually helpful or correspond to predicted forgeries

Single-dataset evaluation with no generalization evidence: Exclusively evaluated on author-constructed MMTT dataset with no cross-dataset validation on existing benchmarks (FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, ForgeryNet)
Limited technical novelty: ForgeryTalker primarily combines existing components (InstructBLIP, SAM, coordinate convolution) with straightforward FPN architecture using standard losses

Annotation quality not rigorously validated: No inter-annotator agreement (IAA) metrics reported; quality control is minimal (false positive screening only); improvement in second annotation phase undocumented
Unfair baseline comparisons: Baseline models not designed for this multi-modal interpretable segmentation task; results are not directly comparable
Limited analysis of results: No failure case analysis, no qualitative examples of generated interpretations with images, missing error analysis and insights into interpretation quality
Scope limitations undermine claims: Synthetic manipulations only (no real deepfakes), only facial images (limited generalization), 512×512 resolution, built on curated datasets

Core interpretability claims unsupported: While claiming interpretable explanations, the weak FPN (41% recall) means most predictions are based on incorrect region guidance, potentially misleading rather than explaining

strengths: Large-scale dataset (128,303 image-text pairs) with careful construction: multiple manipulation types (face swapping, transformer/diffusion inpainting), pixel-level masks, and detailed textual annotations (avg 26.94 words)
Well-designed annotation pipeline with quality control: 1-minute minimum observation, iterative refinement across two phases (Sep-Nov 2023, Mar-Jul 2024), false positive filtering
Comprehensive dataset documentation with detailed statistics on manipulation types, modified facial parts, and caption distributions
Commitment to reproducibility through promised dataset, code, and model checkpoint releases
Clear problem motivation: extending forgery localization beyond binary masks to provide human-understandable interpretations
weaknesses: FUNDAMENTAL VENUE MISALIGNMENT: This is a computer vision/forensics paper, not a computational linguistics paper. Core contributions (forgery detection, localization, dataset) are in vision domain. Should be submitted to CVPR/ICCV/ECCV, not ACL

LIMITED NLP CONTRIBUTION: Text generation uses standard fine-tuning of InstructBLIP with a simple template ('These facial areas may be manipulated by AI: [R]. Please describe...'). No architectural innovations or advanced explanation generation techniques. Text component is secondary/incidental to region detection

INSUFFICIENT EXPLANATION EVALUATION: (a) No human evaluation of explanation quality, faithfulness, or usefulness; (b) BLEU/METEOR/CIDEr metrics are inappropriate for evaluating explanations—these assume reference quality similarity but explanation evaluation requires human judgment; (c) No faithfulness analysis linking explanations to detected regions; (d) Large oracle gap (FPN-GT CIDEr 48.1 vs. actual 21.5, 2.2x difference) indicates region detection bottleneck dominates, not text generation

EXPERIMENTAL LIMITATIONS: (a) All manipulations synthetic (E4S, MAT, SDXL)—no real-world deepfakes; (b) No cross-dataset evaluation (FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF); (c) No inter-annotator agreement (IAA) reported—30 annotators label ~128K images without Cohen's/Fleiss' Kappa; (d) FPN's Positive Label Matching only 41%, indicating weak region detection; (e) Marginal improvements over InstructBLIP baseline (BLEU-2: 16.9 vs 16.8; ROUGE-L: 24.3 vs 24.8)

MISSING CRITICAL EVALUATION METRICS: No measurement of annotation quality/consistency; no human evaluation of generated explanations; no error bars or significance tests; no failure case analysis; no qualitative study of what explanations capture

LIMITED TECHNICAL NOVELTY: ForgeryTalker combines off-the-shelf components (ViT+Conv for FPN, SAM for mask decoder, fine-tuned InstructBLIP for generation). Only coordinate convolution is somewhat novel. Two-stage training is standard. No significant architectural innovations

DATASET QUALITY CONCERNS: (a) Unknown inter-annotator agreement on textual descriptions; (b) Synthetic-only data raises generalization questions; (c) No analysis of annotation disagreements or systematic biases; (d) 4.3K images per annotator with no consistency checks

INCOMPLETE ABLATIONS: (a) No justification for instruction template design; (b) No analysis of explanation quality by manipulation type; (c) Discount factor ω=0.2 appears arbitrary; (d) No isolation of FPN's contribution to text generation vs. localization; (e) No comparison of FPN prompts vs. ground-truth on text quality

WEAK BASELINE COMPARISONS: Most baselines (SCA, Osprey, LISA-7B) are general vision-language models, not forgery-specialized. No comparison with task-specific forgery detection methods. Fair comparison would fine-tune baselines on same task

MISSING GENERALIZATION EVIDENCE: Evaluation only on authors' synthetic dataset; no evidence of performance on real-world deepfakes or other forensics benchmarks; unclear how synthetic-trained model transfers to real forgeries

strengths: Novel problem formulation combining forgery localization with interpretable textual explanations addresses a real need that binary masks cannot satisfy
Large-scale, well-annotated multi-modal dataset (128,303 image-text pairs) with careful annotation pipeline including QC, minimum observation time, and iterative refinement
Comprehensive dataset documentation with detailed statistics on manipulation types, facial regions, and comparison with existing benchmarks
Technically sound architecture combining FPN, mask decoder, and MLLM with reasonable design choices (coordinate convolution for spatial priors, two-stage training)
Solid experimental setup with multiple evaluation metrics, ablation studies demonstrating FPN importance, and commitment to reproducibility
Well-articulated motivation for why binary segmentation masks alone are insufficient for forensic analysis
weaknesses: Critical limitation: No cross-dataset evaluation. Entire evaluation is in-domain (MMTT only); no testing on FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, DeeperForensics, or other forensic benchmarks undermines generalization claims
No human evaluation of interpretation quality despite interpretability being the core contribution. Automatic metrics (CIDEr, BLEU) measure n-gram overlap, not explanation fidelity or usefulness

Severe FPN bottleneck: 41% region detection performance (PLM) with 2.2× performance drop from ground-truth labels (48.1 CIDEr) to predicted labels (21.5 CIDEr). This gap is acknowledged but not investigated

Limited and somewhat unfair baseline comparisons. SCA, LISA-7B, and InstructBLIP are general-purpose models not optimized for this task; no adapted task-specific baselines. SCA actually achieves higher IoU (72.87 vs 70.81)
No qualitative error analysis: missing examples of failure cases, visualization of FPN predictions, or breakdown of which manipulation types/regions are hardest to interpret
Dataset scope limitations: facial images only, three manipulation methods only (E4S, MAT, SDXL), no evaluation on real-world deepfakes or adversarial robustness
No inter-annotator agreement metrics reported; unclear how annotation disagreements were resolved or how to assess annotation reliability
Limited NLP novelty and positioning for ACL venue. Text generation uses standard LLM finetuning; primary contributions are CV-focused (dataset + forgery detection). Better suited for CVPR/ICCV

Incomplete technical details: cross-attention mechanism underspecified, instruction template design not justified, hyperparameter choices (ω=0.2, learning rates) lack ablation, computational cost not discussed
Unconventional 8:1:1 train/val/test split without justification; no confidence intervals, error bars, or hyperparameter tuning methodology explanation

strengths: Novel and well-motivated multimodal task combining forgery localization with natural language explanations, addressing a genuine gap in existing forensic detection methods
Large-scale, high-quality dataset (152,217 samples) with process-derived ground-truth masks ensuring pixel-perfect alignment and human-authored descriptions with rigorous quality control
Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive baselines (both specialist and general-purpose LVLMs), cross-dataset generalization (DQ_F++, SynthScars), and informative ablation studies
Solid baseline architecture with thoughtful design choices (FPN architecture, two-stage training pipeline) and strong empirical results (59.3 CIDEr, 73.67 IoU)
Clear presentation with excellent visualizations and strong reproducibility commitment (code, dataset, and pre-trained weights to be released)
weaknesses: Critical evaluation gap: absence of human evaluation for explanation quality, correctness, and spatial grounding; reference-based metrics (CIDEr, BLEU) designed for generic captioning may not capture explanation fidelity for forensic purposes; dramatic performance drop on SynthScars (2.2 vs. 59.3 CIDEr) raises concerns about metric reliability

Dataset construction lacks inter-annotator agreement (IAA) analysis across 30 annotators; no validation of ground-truth mask alignment with human perception; missing demographic diversity analysis (gender, age, ethnicity) and potential bias evaluation across demographic groups

Limited technical novelty: architecture primarily combines existing components (InstructBLIP, SAM, T5); FPN design is relatively standard; four pretraining losses used but only binary ablation provided; individual loss contributions not analyzed

Incomplete task formulation: omits binary real/fake classification under claim of 'saturation' supported by only two 2025 papers; heavy prompt engineering constrains outputs; no analysis of explanation faithfulness vs. post-hoc rationalization; unclear practical applicability

Insufficient FPN analysis: large gap between w/o FPN (51.7 CIDEr) and w/ FPN-GT (95.1 CIDEr) indicates region prompts are critical but unattainable; limited ablation results; no failure case analysis or investigation of struggle regions

Alignment between modalities not explicitly enforced: no mechanism ensuring text explanations correspond to predicted mask regions; cross-attention between Q-former and FPN doesn't guarantee spatial consistency

Limited qualitative analysis: only 4 example pairs shown; no systematic error categorization; missing analysis of performance by manipulation type during inference; no study of explanation diversity or correspondence to human descriptions

strengths: Large-scale, well-constructed MMTT dataset with 152,217 samples combining process-derived masks and human-authored descriptions with rigorous quality control
Clear task formulation addressing interpretability gap in facial forensics through joint localization and explanation
Strong empirical results with ForgeryTalker achieving 59.3 CIDEr and 73.67 IoU, outperforming adapted baselines like InstructBLIP
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablation studies, manipulation type analysis, and generalization to multiple datasets (DQ_F++, SynthScars)
Thorough transparency commitments regarding code, data, and model release for reproducibility
Well-presented paper with clear methodology and informative visualizations
weaknesses: Poor fit for ACL: Fundamentally a computer vision paper on facial forgery detection with minimal NLP contribution. Text generation component is functional but not linguistically novel—uses standard T5-based decoder from InstructBLIP without advancing computational linguistics methodology
Methodological novelty limited to engineering combination of existing components (InstructBLIP encoder + SAM decoder + standard training objectives). No novel generation techniques or NLP innovations

Dataset limitations undermine contribution: (1) Entirely synthetic manipulations with unknown real-world performance gap; (2) Only 4 manipulation types; (3) Critical omission of inter-annotator agreement metrics; (4) No inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa) despite NLP task; (5) 512×512 resolution below modern standards; (6) No demographic bias analysis

Text quality validation insufficient: No human evaluation of generated explanations; Low BLEU-4 (12.5) suggests poor n-gram overlap; No grounding verification that explanations match predicted masks; No error analysis of failure modes; Potential artifact memorization not investigated

Concerning FPN dependency: Model drops from 59.3 to 51.7 CIDEr without FPN, and oracle FPN reaches 95.1 CIDEr, indicating the model relies heavily on accurate region prompts rather than learning robust multimodal representations—suggests weak end-to-end learning
Task motivation weakened by circular reasoning (citing concurrent work on saturation); No user study validating that explanations are actually useful for practitioners compared to masks alone

Missing critical implementation details: Annotator training procedures not described; inter-rater reliability unreported; annotation cost/timeline absent; how '1-minute minimum observation' enforced unclear
All evaluation on synthetic data only (MMTT, DQ_F++, SynthScars all synthetic). No cross-domain evaluation on real manipulations or out-of-distribution attacks
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals for reported metrics; Limited error analysis by manipulation type; Only 4 qualitative examples shown in Figure 6
Narrow scope limited to facial manipulation with unclear generalization to other object categories or diverse attack types

strengths: Novel task formulation: Forgery Attribution Report Generation meaningfully combines localization with natural language explanation, addressing a genuine gap in forensics interpretability

High-quality, well-designed dataset: 152,217 samples with process-derived pixel-perfect masks, rigorous human annotation quality control (1-min minimum observation, automated false-positive flagging), and rich linguistic annotations (4M+ words). First dataset combining detailed textual explanations with forgery localization

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive ablations (FPN contribution, pretraining stage, manipulation types), cross-dataset validation (strong generalization to DQ_F++), multiple metrics, and comparisons against both zero-shot LVLMs and fine-tuned specialist models
Strong empirical results with clear improvements: 59.3 CIDEr (vs 51.7 InstructBLIP), 73.67 IoU; demonstrates complementary effects between localization and generation tasks
Well-designed FPN architecture: Parallel ViT and convolution branches with coordinate convolution provide good balance of global and local context for detecting forgeries
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations, detailed methodology, explicit commitments to release code/data/weights, comprehensive experimental setup
Ethical awareness: Acknowledges dual-use risks and proposes controlled release policy with Data Usage Agreement and access restrictions
weaknesses: No human evaluation of core interpretability claim: Despite claiming explanations improve interpretability and trust, paper lacks user studies validating that generated explanations are actually more trustworthy or help humans detect forgeries better than masks alone. Missing trust metrics and qualitative feedback

Insufficient annotation quality documentation: No inter-annotator agreement metrics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa) reported. 30 annotators for 152,217 samples (~5,000 per annotator) raises consistency concerns. No analysis of annotator bias, fatigue, or linguistic diversity across annotators

Limited technical novelty: Heavy reliance on existing components (InstructBLIP, SAM, Q-former) without substantial modification. FPN is relatively straightforward (parallel branches). Two-stage training adds complexity but yields only modest improvement (54.4→59.3 CIDEr, +5%)
Large unexplained FPN oracle gap: Oracle performance (95.1 CIDEr) vs learned (59.3 CIDEr) is substantial but poorly analyzed. Missing investigation into why learned FPN underperforms so significantly

Dataset limitations and bias concerns: (1) Narrow scope—only facial forgeries; (2) Limited source diversity—only CelebA-HQ + FFHQ (predominantly frontal celebrity faces); (3) No demographic bias analysis; (4) Only 3 manipulation paradigms; (5) 512×512 resolution is dated by 2026 standards; (6) Cross-dataset results show significant domain shift (CIDEr 2.2 on SynthScars)

Missing critical ablations and analyses: No ablation on individual pretraining losses (λ weights stated as 'empirically tuned' but not shown); missing analysis of why coordinate convolution helps; no ablation on instruction template design; no error analysis or performance breakdown by facial region

Weak evaluation methodology: (1) No automatic metric for text interpretability; (2) Process-derived masks are perfect by construction—doesn't test robustness to imperfect annotations; (3) CIDEr metric based on n-gram matching may not capture semantic quality; (4) No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Two-stage training complexity not justified: Would single-stage end-to-end training perform comparably? Not tested. Adds unnecessary complexity if marginal gains justify it

Limited scope for ACL venue: Work is more suited to computer vision or multimodal conferences (CVPR/ICCV/ICLR). NLP component is secondary—mostly uses existing LLMs for generation rather than proposing novel NLP methods. Limited contribution to core NLP tasks

Reproducibility gaps despite commitments: Dependencies on frozen pretrained models; some hyperparameter choices not fully specified; full reproduction requires dataset access; coordinate convolution implementation details missing
